status_policy: Ready means all dependencies are done; optional external work also requires explicit authorization. A coordinator serializes claims and status updates. Done requires an evidence handoff and the checks in AGENTS.md.

tasks.title: Configure and pin the Lean environment
acceptance: Select and record an exact Lean/Mathlib pair after finite symmetric-polynomial, weighted-grading, tensor, and Hopf import probes.
Build all accepted modules and check root coverage; prove the check catches an intentionally broken scratch module without shipping that module.
Verify Lean MCP discovery/search/diagnostics or record a working CLI fallback.
Implement task-DAG and no-placeholder prechecks; document the separate transitive-axiom check.
Record colleague port compatibility and attribution requirements.

tasks.title: Define the polynomial-backed public type
acceptance: Choose and document a dedicated type backed by MvPolynomial ℕ+ R; test wrapper versus controlled type synonym before freezing it.
Provide ring/algebra instances, the polynomial algebra equivalence, e : ℕ → SymmetricFunction R, and e 0 = 1.
Provide evaluation into a commutative R-algebra, generator evaluation laws, induction, and algebra-map extensionality.
Demonstrate ordinary algebra elaboration without unfolding the representation downstream.

tasks.title: Equate partitions with weighted exponent vectors
acceptance: Construct Nat.Partition d ≃ {a : ℕ+ →₀ ℕ // ∑ i in a.support, (i : ℕ) * a i = d}.
Prove both inverse laws and product/multiplicity interpretation, including the empty partition.
Reuse Mathlib Nat.Partition; do not import the colleague's redeclaration.

tasks.title: Transport weighted grading and degree filtration
acceptance: Construct homogeneous components, direct-sum decomposition, and degree-at-most submodules.
Prove e n is homogeneous of degree n and multiplication respects grading.
Handle degree zero and the zero coefficient ring without global Nontrivial assumptions.

tasks.title: Construct the elementary partition basis
acceptance: Port or reconstruct the general weighted monomial basis lemma with source attribution.
Construct a Basis (Nat.Partition d) R of the degree-d component with vector e_μ.
Give coefficient and product formulas and the all-partitions basis via direct sum.

tasks.title: Prove coefficient functoriality and scalar extension
acceptance: Construct coefficient maps for ring homomorphisms and identity/composition laws.
Construct R ⊗[ℤ] SymmetricFunction ℤ ≃ₐ[R] SymmetricFunction R.
Prove evaluation and elementary-generator compatibility; do not infer a lambda structure from CommRing R.

tasks.title: Specialize to finite symmetric polynomials
acceptance: Construct rho_N as an R-algebra map into MvPolynomial.symmetricSubalgebra (Fin N) R.
Construct zero-last-variable transitions and prove compatibility on all elements.
Prove elementary evaluation, vanishing for indices greater than N, and empty-alphabet formulas.

tasks.title: Prove weighted finite fundamental theorem and stable range
acceptance: Prove weighted-homogeneous compatibility of the finite elementary presentation using Mathlib's fundamental theorem.
Prove rho_N is surjective and identify its kernel as the ideal generated by e k for k > N.
For N ≥ d, construct the degree-at-most-d R-linear equivalence and a bounded-degree equality test.
State explicitly why the result does not assert global injectivity of rho_N.

tasks.title: Identify bounded compatible families
acceptance: Define compatible symmetric polynomial families with a single uniform existential degree bound.
Prove ring closure, construct the algebra equivalence to SymmetricFunction R, and verify each specialization.
Prove independence of the chosen bound and stable alphabet.

tasks.title: Construct complete symmetric functions integrally
acceptance: Define h recursively with h 0 = 1 and the finite coefficient recurrence E(-u)H(u) = 1.
Prove homogeneity and both convolution orders without dividing by integers.
Provide the generator recurrence API needed for omega and the antipode.

tasks.title: Construct the elementary-complete involution
acceptance: Define the algebra map e n ↦ h n.
Prove omega(h n) = e n and package an involutive algebra equivalence preserving degree.

tasks.title: Transport the complete partition basis
acceptance: Construct the homogeneous and all-partitions complete bases through omega.
Prove polynomial freeness of h generators and basis evaluation formulas.

tasks.title: Construct positive power sums and finite compatibility
acceptance: Define positive power sums using integral Newton recurrences.
Prove specialization of h and p to Mathlib hsymm and psum; prove homogeneity.
Verify p_2 = e_1^2 - 2e_2 and do not introduce a stable cardinal-valued p_0.

tasks.title: Prove the standard Hopf algebra structure
acceptance: Construct comultiplication, counit, and antipode with the elementary-generator formulas from ROADMAP.
Prove both antipode laws, coassociativity, counit laws, and instantiate Mathlib HopfAlgebra.
Prove complete coproduct, primitive positive power sums, cocommutativity, connected grading, and coefficient-map compatibility.
Check tensor base rings and associators explicitly.

tasks.title: Construct stable integral product and iteration polynomials
acceptance: Define product polynomials from elementary functions of pairwise products in two alphabets.
Define iteration polynomials from elementary functions of squarefree degree-m monomials.
Prove uniqueness, sufficient-variable bounds, truncation stability, degree bounds, and boundary conventions.
Keep this construction independent of any lambda structure on SymmetricFunction.

tasks.title: Define pre-lambda and special lambda rings
acceptance: Define the exterior-power convention with zero, one, addition, unit, product, and iteration laws.
Define preserving ring morphisms, composition, identity, and extensionality.
Document arbitrary torsion targets and explicit index-zero cases; review every universal polynomial substitution.

tasks.title: Construct lambda operations on integer polynomial rings
acceptance: Define finite products of (1 + m u)^a using units and integer exponents in one-variable power series.
Prove addition, unit normalization, lambda_1 identity, and negative-coefficient formulas.
Prove renaming and zero-variable-substitution naturality plus degree(lambda_k f) ≤ k*d when degree(f) ≤ d.
Do not claim the special identities in this task.

tasks.title: Prove both special identities including virtual differences
acceptance: Write a reviewed decomposition of the product and iteration identity proofs before extended search.
Prove both universal identities for arbitrary integer polynomial coefficients, including negative ones.
Package the finite integer polynomial special lambda-ring instance and preserving substitution maps.
If using a torsion-free Adams criterion, prove that criterion and its hypotheses rather than assuming it.

tasks.title: Transport integral lambda operations through stability
acceptance: Show finite operations preserve symmetric families, compatibility, and a uniform degree bound.
Transfer the special structure to SymmetricFunction ℤ.
Prove lambda_n(e_1) = e_n and compatibility with finite integer specializations.

tasks.title: Prove the free special lambda-ring universal property
acceptance: For arbitrary special lambda ring A and a : A, construct the ring map e n ↦ lambda_n(a).
Prove preservation of all lambda operations on arbitrary expressions using special identities.
Prove uniqueness and package Hom_lambda(SymmetricFunction ℤ,A) ≃ A with evaluation and naturality laws.
Review that the result has no torsion-free assumption on A and does not assume the desired morphism exists.

tasks.title: Integrate and audit the initial deliverable
acceptance: Build every accepted module and affected downstream examples in the pinned environment.
Review the exact stable-realization, Hopf, and free-lambda theorem statements against the mathematical targets.
Audit transitive axioms and absence of proof holes, including reused modules.
Check zero-degree, empty alphabet, e/h/p identities, e_2 coproduct, antipode, and lambda-generator examples.
Publish a local declaration index and identify genuinely unfinished extensions without presenting them as initial-release gaps.

tasks.title: Derive integral plethysm and alphabet operations
acceptance: Define plethysm from lambda evaluation and prove unit and associativity laws.
Derive Adams operations and psi_k(p_n) = p_(kn).
Prove needed tensor-product lambda structure before claiming compatibility with Hopf alphabet addition.

tasks.title: Support rational evaluation and multiple alphabets
acceptance: Prove the power-sum polynomial presentation and basis over a Q-algebra.
Construct evaluation from specified power-sum images; distinguish fixed outer coefficients and parameter Adams action.
Prove sign and parameter conventions, including p_k[-X] and p_k[tX].
Construct separately symmetric tensor alphabets and mixed finite-polynomial/symmetric objects; state hypotheses for X/(1-t) evaluation.

tasks.title: Construct the monomial basis and coefficient extraction
acceptance: Lift finite monomial symmetric polynomials through stability.
Prove the homogeneous partition basis and finite-specialization coefficient formulas.
Adapt useful exponent-orbit arguments from SymmetricFun without replacing Mathlib partitions.

tasks.title: Identify bounded symmetric power series
acceptance: Port selected homogeneous and permutation-action lemmas with attribution.
Prove SymmetricFunction R is algebra-equivalent to bounded symmetric MvPowerSeries ℕ R.
Prove compatibility for e, h, m and finite specializations; close all transitive holes in reused proofs.

tasks.title: Develop Schur and Hall theory
acceptance: Split into smaller reviewed tasks for Jacobi–Trudi, basis, conjugation/omega, Hall pairing, skewing, and Cauchy identities.
Use an explicit integer-index extension of h for determinant formulas.
Retain proof links to combinatorial definitions needed for later positivity results.

tasks.title: Support symmetric series and convergent substitutions
acceptance: Construct the product of homogeneous components with convolution multiplication.
Define Omega and prove the e/h generating-series identities in the completion.
State and prove sufficient continuity/substitution conditions, including completed tensor products for coproduct extension.
Do not claim arbitrary infinite plethysm exists.

tasks.title: Render the mathematical proof dependency plan
acceptance: Connect prose statements and proofs to exact declarations using Lean Blueprint.
Use task IDs and declaration mappings consistently; distinguish planned, formalized, and proved nodes.
Do not block local theorem work on successful website rendering.

tasks.title: Evaluate a small Prove2Me proof workflow
acceptance: Run only after explicit authorization for external work.
Select one reviewed stable leaf and an explicit compatible verification environment.
Record theorem/definition IDs, source hashes, and the reversible local-name mapping.
Retrieve a closed proof and recompile locally; measure integration effort before expanding the pilot.
